chunks: Verily there are signs in this; yet many of them do not believe.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean when it says 'there are signs in this' but 'most of them do not believe'?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Ash-Shu'ara, this verse underscores the paradox of divine clarity versus human obstinacy, a central theme in Shia exegesis where 'signs' (ayat) are abundant yet faith remains rare due to spiritual heedlessness. It reflects the historical reality of the Prophet's time, where the majority of Quraysh rejected the message despite witnessing clear miracles, illustrating that intellectual recognition does not automatically equate to sincere belief.
